verdict.rationale: Snowflake provides native event-driven automation primitives — Streams capture DML changes so 'actions can be taken using the changed data' (snowflake-docs-7/21/38/54), Snowpipe auto-loads data as files arrive (snowflake-docs-6/20/29/34/44), and Resource Monitors/anomaly alerts trigger suspend or notification actions on threshold events (snowflake-docs-53/60/17/33). These are genuine rule-trigger-action mechanisms usable by any user including AI-native ones, but the evidence never frames this as a user-facing 'define a rule, agent executes on event' capability tailored for AI-native workflows, and there's no explicit task/orchestration scheduler doc shown. Missing for 10: explicit Tasks/orchestration docs pairing Streams for full CDC-to-action pipelines, and any AI-agent-specific rule-authoring interface beyond generic SQL-based automation.
